p1-v1.alt: Two rockets lift off from Earth into space; a rover travels inside each one.

textos.texto: The year is 2003. NASA launches twin missions to explore Mars. Spirit and Opportunity begin their long journey.

p1-v2.alt: Spirit, with orange details, and Opportunity, with teal details, smile at each other inside the spacecraft.

textos.texto: Hi, brother! I'm so excited to reach Mars.
Me too, Spirit! We're going to discover so much.

p1-v3.alt: A probe descends by parachute over Mars while a cluster of airbags bounces on the ground.

textos.texto: January 2004. Each rover arrived wrapped in airbags that bounced across the ground until they came to a stop.

p1-v4.alt: The two happy rovers on the red ground of Mars, with mountains behind them.

textos.texto: We made it! We're on Mars!
Look how red everything is! Let's explore!

p2-v1.alt: Opportunity's robotic arm examines a layered rock; a magnifying glass shows the layers up close.

textos.texto: Opportunity found layered rocks and tiny hematite spheres: clues that there was water here long ago.

p2-v2.alt: Spirit in the distance and Opportunity in the foreground, each in a different part of Mars.

textos.texto: I'm in Gusev Crater, on the other side of Mars.
And I'm still looking for signs of water!

p2-v3.alt: A dust devil spins behind Spirit, whose solar panels are covered in dust.

textos.texto: Phew, so much dust! My solar panels are dirty and I have less energy.

p2-v4.alt: A calendar with many crossed-out days next to the two rovers on Mars.

textos.texto: The mission was planned to last about 90 Martian days. Spirit worked for more than 6 years, and Opportunity for more than 14!

p3-v1.alt: Spirit, with its wheels sunk in the sand, thinks about Earth.

textos.texto: In 2009, Spirit got stuck in soft sand. It kept studying the ground without moving until its last signal, in 2010.

p3-v2.alt: Opportunity, alone, on a field of rippled dunes.

textos.texto: I'll miss you, Spirit. I'll keep exploring for both of us.

p3-v3.alt: A dust storm darkens the sky; Opportunity can barely be seen.

textos.texto: In 2018, a dust storm covered the whole planet. Without sunlight, Opportunity ran out of power and stopped communicating.

p3-v4.alt: Spirit and Opportunity under a starry sky; Earth waves at them from above and there is a plaque on the ground.

textos.texto: Thanks to Spirit and Opportunity, we know Mars had water long ago. Their legacy lives on in the new explorers.

cierre.datoReal: Opportunity traveled more than 45 kilometers (28 miles) on Mars: farther than a marathon.
cierre.preguntaAula: Why do you think the rovers worked so much longer than planned?
